title: Permanent Gene Repression by CRISPR-Adenine Base Editing of Promoter CCAAT Motifs
author: Daliri, Clement
materials: This section outlines the preparation of cell lysates for gDNA extraction suitable for Sanger sequencing, including an efficient lysis buffer recipe for small-scale samples.Note: For extracting DNA from a small number of cells, you can use e lysis buffer for sequencing applications. DNA extraction with this solution involves simple cell lysis without the need for subsequent purification.37.Mix proteinase K (NEB) into the cell lysis buffer at a dilution ratio of 1:1,000 (vol/vol).CRITICAL: Store proteinase K at −20°C for up to 12 months.38.Add lysis buffer directly to plates from Step 30.Pause point: In general, 150 μl of lysis buffer is sufficient for each well of a 24-well plate.39.Incubate the plates at 37°C for 1 hour.40.Transfer the lysis mixture to PCR strips and deactivate the proteinase K by heating at 80°C for 20 minutes.CRITICAL: The DNA can be temporarily stored at 8°C for two weeks or frozen at −80°C for months.41.Assess the quality and quantity of the extracted DNA using a NanoDrop spectrophotometer.Note: The concentration of the isolated DNA of 50–100 ng/μl indicates an acceptable yield.CRITICAL: The absorbance ratios (260/280 nm) should range from 1.8 to 2.2.42.Perform Sanger sequencing of the product using the same sequencing primers (Keep diluted primers in −20°C for 6 months) used to sequence the genomic target site (Steps 1–10) in unedited NIH3T3.43.Determine base editing efficiencies from Sanger sequence chromatograms using EditR.

steps.title: Prepare lysis buffer with Proteinase K
steps.instruction: Mix Proteinase K (NEB) into the cell lysis buffer at a 1:1,000 (vol/vol) dilution; store Proteinase K at –20 °C for up to 12 months.

steps.title: Lyse cells and incubate
steps.instruction: Add 150 µL of the prepared lysis buffer directly to each well of a 24‑well plate, then incubate the plate at 37 °C for 1 hour.

steps.title: Deactivate Proteinase K
steps.instruction: Transfer the lysate to PCR strips and heat at 80 °C for 20 minutes to inactivate Proteinase K; DNA may be stored at 8 °C for up to 2 weeks or at –80 °C for longer periods.

steps.title: Assess DNA quality and quantity
steps.instruction: Measure DNA concentration with a NanoDrop; acceptable yield is 50–100 ng/µL and 260/280 absorbance ratio should be 1.8–2.2.

steps.title: Perform Sanger sequencing
steps.instruction: Submit the DNA for Sanger sequencing using the same primers employed for the original genomic target (keep diluted primers at –20 °C for up to 6 months).

steps.title: Calculate editing efficiency
steps.instruction: Analyze the Sanger chromatograms with EditR to determine base‑editing efficiencies.

steps.title: Dissociate transfected cells
steps.instruction: 48 h post‑transfection, add 0.05 % Trypsin‑EDTA to each well, incubate at 37 °C for 3–5 minutes, gently pipette to detach cells, pass the suspension through a cell‑strainer cap, and verify single‑cell suspension microscopically.

steps.title: Prepare limiting‑dilution suspension
steps.instruction: Count cells and dilute in DMEM to achieve 0.5 cells per 100 µL (e.g., 70 cells in 12 mL per 96‑well plate); prepare at least three 96‑well plates per transfected population.

steps.title: Plate cells by limiting dilution
steps.instruction: Using a multichannel pipette, dispense 100 µL of the diluted suspension into each well of the 96‑well plates; place plates in a 37 °C CO₂ incubator.

steps.title: Monitor colony formation
steps.instruction: Inspect wells after ~1 week for clonal‑appearing colonies; return plates to the incubator and allow colonies to expand for ~2 weeks.

steps.title: Passage colonies
steps.instruction: After 2 weeks, split each colony into a new 96‑well plate at a 1:2 ratio (duplicate wells); incubate for 3–4 days.

steps.title: Genotype colonies
steps.instruction: Extract genomic DNA from one well of each duplicate, amplify the target region by PCR, and perform Sanger sequencing as described earlier to confirm the desired mutation.

steps.title: Assess off‑target editing
steps.instruction: PCR‑amplify the top three predicted off‑target loci (identified with Cas‑OFFinder using default S. pyogenes Cas9 parameters) and Sanger‑sequence them as above.

steps.title: Analyze qPCR melt curves
steps.instruction: Run melt‑curve analysis at the end of qPCR; verify a single sharp peak indicating specific primer annealing.

steps.title: Quantify expression and test significance
steps.instruction: Use the instrument’s software to calculate Ct values, apply the 2‑ΔΔCt method (normalize to GAPDH), export data to Excel/GraphPad Prism, and perform unpaired two‑tailed t‑tests; report mean ± SD, with p < 0.05 considered significant.
